title: Canonical matching schemes and comparison of hypercover predicates
statement: For a simplicial object U in the small etale category of X, define its degree n matching scheme as the finite limit indexed by all maps [m] to [n] with m<n. It has the projections, simplicial matching map, naturality and universal property used in the etale hypercover predicate [def-weil-pbc-etale-hypercover]. The same cone restricted to injective proper faces [lem-weil-pbc-matching-object-proper-faces] is limiting. An etale hypercover has surjective canonical matching maps, and after the singleton inclusion it is a semi-representable hypercover [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object].

source.place: Tag 0186, matching objects; finite etale limits and the singleton matching comparison

proof.text: The lower-simplex index has finitely many objects and finite hom sets. Its opposite domain diagram in X.Etale has a finite limit. Its projections and the cone of simplicial operators define the matching arrow. The etale inclusion preserves finite limits, proving the universal property among all schemes over X. A simplicial map induces a map of these matching limits by its component maps.

To compare with proper faces, extend every proper-face cone to all lower simplices by their canonical epi-mono image factorizations. Naturality of the image factorization gives compatibility. On a proper face this extension is the original cone, and on an arbitrary simplex its value is forced by the image face. Thus the restricted canonical cone is limiting.

Given any matching witnesses from the hypercover predicate, use their universal property and the canonical limit to obtain a split comparison map onto the canonical matching scheme. The matching arrows commute with this map, so surjectivity passes to the canonical arrow.

Apply the singleton proper-face matching comparison. Its limiting cone and the canonical proper-face cone are uniquely isomorphic. Their matching arrows commute with this isomorphism, so canonical surjectivity implies the singleton semi-representable hypercover predicate.
